newsitem.title: USA: Ford idles light truck lines as planned.
newsitem.headline: Ford idles light truck lines as planned.

text.p: Ford Motor Co as planned closed light truck assembly lines at three plants late Thursday and early Friday in Michigan and Ohio after the United Auto Workers and seat supplier Johnson Controls Inc failed to settle a strike.
The shutdown suspended all production at Ford's Michigan Assembly in Wayne, which makes the Ford Expedition full size sport/utility and F-Series pickup trucks.
Ohio plants affected were the van assembly line in Lorain and a frame production line at Ohio Assembly in Avon Lake. About 6,800 workers were idled as a result of the action.

About 500 UAW members struck Johnson Controls seat plants January 28 in Plymouth, Mich., and Oberlin, Ohio, when talks broke down on a new contract. The plants do final assembly of seats for the Expedition and Econoline vans.
Ford refused to accept seats made by non-union replacements, but decided to keep producing the Expeditions and Econolines with temporary seats in hope that a resolution would be reached.

When the strike, now in its 11th day, dragged on, Ford decided it would be too hard for Johnson Controls to catch up with the approximately 14,800 vans and Expeditions already made as well as meet ongoing needs.

Ford spokesman Bert Serre said the company has been making a limited number of front seats, less than 20 an hour, for the Expedition at its Chesterfield, Mich., trim plant. But there are no plans to make second and third row seats, he said.
Workers idled at the Michigan Truck receive between half and 95 percent of their regular pay, depending on the state and regular benefits they are eligible for.
A recorded message on a Johnson Controls anwering machine said no settlement had been reached. It was unclear if talks were still ongoing.
